title: Local Agent authority architecture
summary: How desktop, remote, and session-scoped clients reach one Electron-main Agent authority, its crash-recoverable Workspace consent and active Project to Workspace ownership chain, and reviewed Codex or Claude provider processes.

chapters.title: Desktop command path
chapters.summary: A structured Agent panel crosses the isolated preload into the single local command authority.

chapters.title: Durable session ownership
chapters.summary: The authority persists exact external Workspace consent separately from the active Project and Workspace graph, then retires descendant capabilities atomically before provider work is projected back.

chapters.title: Reviewed provider boundary
chapters.summary: One provider-neutral state machine selects a reviewed executable and speaks either Codex app-server or Claude Agent SDK.

chapters.title: Additional clients
chapters.summary: Authenticated Android v12, project-scoped local CLI, and per-session MCP capabilities reuse the same command authority without gaining desktop provider administration.

nodes.label: Structured Agent workbench
nodes.detail: A draft becomes a durable Agent on first send; users can open and control managed child Sessions directly.

evidence.claim: The structured panel sends typed submit commands and creates the durable Agent only when the draft's first prompt is submitted.
The active relation and direct-child list let the user open a managed child as its own structured Session surface.
The Session surface wires submit, interrupt-and-submit, settings, approvals, related-session opening, and managed cancel, archive, or detach actions.

nodes.label: Authenticated Android v12
nodes.detail: Authenticated revisioned daemon projection for remote snapshots, transcripts, commands, and events; successful launch and resume records retain exact target or history identity.

evidence.claim: The remote bridge binds an authenticated Android identity to each parsed v12 daemon command and returns the authority receipt.
The remote history source records a successful launch with its exact target and a successful resume with its exact history identity.

nodes.label: Project-scoped local CLI
nodes.detail: An authenticated loopback capability exposes bounded Project commands only while its source Session and complete Project and Workspace ownership chain remain active.

evidence.claim: Every recognized CLI route obtains a Project scope before returning a filtered snapshot or dispatching a mutation.
Project scope requires a live source Session and the shared active Project and Workspace chain, rejects mismatched or expired capabilities, and limits ids to that Project.

nodes.label: Isolated preload bridge
nodes.detail: Only named availability, snapshot, transcript, command, event, and provider-review APIs cross context isolation.

evidence.claim: Preload exposes the bounded daemon client and desktop-only provider setup methods through named IPC calls.

nodes.label: Electron-main user daemon
nodes.detail: Electron main owns terminal/provider processes and Project/Workspace mutation, recovers consent before Agent startup, cleans capabilities, and treats windows as optional.

evidence.claim: DaemonRuntime defines Electron main as the user-level process owner while renderer windows remain optional clients.
Only after Project preflight and ordered MCP, Agent, and automation startup does main publish ready availability; any failure is cleaned up and latched as terminal-only safe mode.
The closeable Project FIFO serializes discovery and fresh-snapshot sync, propagates cancellation, and passes reactivation ids only for explicit user intent.

nodes.label: Revisioned command router
nodes.detail: One FIFO validates principals, idempotency, active ownership, provider-native ownership, outbox state, and commits; system planners evaluate against its latest snapshot.

evidence.claim: The router strictly parses every command, serializes accepted work, and can close external ingress without discarding its accepted FIFO prefix.
Authorization, idempotency, outbox delivery state, durable commit, and event publication remain inside one exclusive command transaction.
A system transition planner derives its commit from the fresh snapshot only after entering the same serialized router gate.

nodes.label: SQLite Project Workspace Session graph
nodes.detail: The durable graph owns Projects, Workspaces and archive state, Sessions, Agents, managed relations, turns, transcripts, approvals, and automation records.

evidence.claim: The v12 contract gives every Workspace a Project and every Session a Project and Workspace, then attaches Agent, relation, and turn records.
The SQLite owner enables foreign keys and WAL with full synchronization, migrates, recovers uncertain commands, and publishes ready state only afterward.
The same revisioned snapshot contains transcript heads, approvals, reviewed Providers, schedules, heartbeats, and runtime settings beside the Session graph.

nodes.label: Active Workspace authority
nodes.detail: One shared predicate requires an unarchived Workspace, requested Project match, and unarchived owning Project before Session, Agent, CLI, MCP, or automation admission and claiming.

evidence.claim: The shared lookup returns a Workspace only when it is active, matches any requested Project, and its owning Project exists and is active.
Schedule creation, enabled updates, and run-now admission all require the shared active Project and Workspace ownership predicate.
Due-run claiming invokes inactive-owner mutations and skips the schedule when the shared ownership gate no longer resolves.

nodes.label: External Workspace consent journal
nodes.detail: A bounded atomic JSON journal keeps external Workspace approval and revocation fail closed across crashes; v1 grants migrate and approval recovery rechecks canonical identity.

evidence.claim: The store strictly bounds and validates v2 grants and pending intents, rejects orphan revocations, and migrates valid v1 grants into an empty journal.
Any pending approval or revocation denies access while atomic begin, exact commit, stale-approval discard, and revoke completion preserve the crash boundary.
Approval and recovery rediscover the exact external worktree, recheck repository and canonical path with cancellation, while revocation recovery remains executable without Git discovery.

nodes.label: Managed Agent state machine
nodes.detail: The runtime owns durable queues, cancel versus interrupt, recovery, tree limits, approvals, timeouts, serialized Provider activation, and active ownership admission.

evidence.claim: One runtime exposes Agent and provider handlers, rehydrates durable state at startup, and serializes provider events back through system transitions.
Cancel commits every queued turn as interrupted and clears the queue; the adjacent turn-scoped interrupt contract explicitly preserves queued successors and the Provider Session.
Provider disable commits unavailable state before advancing its generation, revoking Session capabilities, and deactivating the captured adapter; re-enable pumps only the current generation.

nodes.label: Session-scoped Agent MCP
nodes.detail: A memory-only loopback bearer is bound to a Session and Project, requires an active owner and Provider on every call, and is revoked for either identity before cleanup.

evidence.claim: The loopback authority issues a memory-only bearer only for a live managed Session, binds its Project, and revokes one Session, every capability for a Project, or all capabilities on stop.
Each request rechecks the active Project and Workspace chain, owner, Session, orchestration, and Provider readiness before applying the owner's permission ceiling.

nodes.label: Reviewed provider registry
nodes.detail: Discovery, review binding, health, model lookup, and enabled adapter selection are separate from Agent lifecycle state.

evidence.claim: The provider registry deliberately hides executable discovery, authentication, and protocol-specific process details from the Agent runtime.
Enablement re-probes and compares the complete reviewed executable identity before persisting a ready provider and binding its launch descriptor.

nodes.label: Codex app-server adapter
nodes.detail: A reviewed Codex executable provides persistent app-server threads, generation-fenced transport, pre-response lifecycle correlation, and turn cancellation.

evidence.claim: Codex creates a persistent app-server thread rooted in the selected Workspace and registers its handle only if the Provider lifecycle generation is still current.
The turn-start response establishes ownership, then replays pre-response started, completed, or error events before dispatching a deferred interrupt; failures carry local turn scope.
Deactivation advances the lifecycle, settles pending interrupts, clears approvals and thread ownership, closes app-server, and leaves reviewed configuration reusable.

nodes.label: Claude Agent SDK adapter
nodes.detail: Pinned SDK queries run the reviewed Claude executable with persistent identity and a serialized, generation-fenced reusable lifecycle.

evidence.claim: Claude SDK receives Workspace cwd, reviewed executable, permissions, optional Session MCP, and persistent identity, then installs its query only under the current lifecycle generation.
Deactivation advances the serialized lifecycle and closes every live SDK query, while permanent disposal separately clears listeners after that drain.
Desktop Agent surfaces reach snapshots, transcripts, commands, and events only through the named preload API.
Main resolves the desktop Session principal, bounds transcript reads, gates safe mode, and overwrites the command principal before execution.
No operational remote frame is accepted before bearer or one-shot pairing authentication and exact v12 client negotiation complete.
CLI mutations receive a Session-bound CLI principal and current expected revision, then execute through the shared daemon authority with bounded conflict retries.
Main wires the provider-neutral Agent and automation handlers into one DaemonCommandRouter backed by the SQLite store.
The Project FIFO persists approval or revocation intent before changing daemon authority, finalizes consent afterward, compensates failed approval, and recovers pending work before provider startup.
Each local CLI request expires when its source Session no longer resolves through the shared active Workspace and owning Project gate.
The router binds idempotency, persists provider-dispatch intent, atomically commits or rejects the command, then publishes resulting events.
Project removal, Project save, root removal, and exact external Workspace revocation retire their affected authority and durable descendants through fresh-snapshot transitions.
Sync preserves native tombstones without explicit reactivation, archives missing worktrees only after complete discovery, and fails before mutation when discovery is unavailable.

Project save stops active orchestration when authority shrinks, retires obsolete daemon descendants and capabilities, clears removed consent and auxiliary authority, then publishes and explicitly reactivates the replacement.
Full removal stops Project runs, applies the fail-closed daemon transition, revokes MCP and Agent-control tokens, and only then removes consent, coordination, orchestration, and history records.
The authority predicate reads the current graph and returns only a matching active Workspace whose owning Project is also active.
Agent creation and resume require a Workspace that resolves through the requested active Project before any durable Agent state is accepted.
Turn submission revalidates the Session's complete active Project and Workspace ownership chain.
The queue pump rechecks active Project and Workspace ownership before claiming or delivering a durable turn.
Project archive atomically archives child Workspaces, while Session creation admits only a Workspace under the requested active Project.
Every MCP capability use rechecks the owner's active Project and Workspace chain before Session and Provider authorization.
Launch, resume, and Project or worker activity records enter the same main-owned FIFO; only direct-directory launch conveys explicit Project re-registration intent before sync.
Project-target launches and indexed resume history only touch existing Projects, while a direct-directory launch returns its deterministic Project id as explicit registration intent.
Provider observations honor the most-specific active or revoked Project and Workspace authority, import only unknown canonical paths, and sync before leaving the FIFO.
DaemonAgentRuntime receives only snapshot, durable transition, transcript, command, and orchestration capability seams before its handlers join the router.
Startup expires approvals, repairs unattached claims, rehydrates provider Sessions, reconciles unsettled work, rearms timeouts, and resumes the queue.
An orchestration-enabled managed Session receives only its own loopback MCP descriptor in the provider context.
MCP tools create direct children within the owner's permission ceiling and reauthorize managed-descendant commands against the latest revision before mutation.

The FIFO claims one durable turn only through the complete active Project and Workspace chain, waits the Provider lifecycle barrier, rechecks state and the enabled adapter, then invokes the provider-neutral Session contract.
The provider-neutral error event can identify a local turn, a Provider turn, or both, while leaving Session-wide failures explicitly unscoped.
Scoped errors resolve one active turn and mutate Agent and Session only when current; recoverable scoped or Session-wide errors preserve an existing interrupt fence.
Late interrupt failure commits delivery-uncertain only when the expected turn is still current and non-terminal, preventing stale callbacks from corrupting successors.
Codex accepts only an absolute reviewed app-server launch descriptor and reports the capabilities and version that review covered.
Claude accepts only the reviewed SDK executable contract and persists consent policy without implementing an OAuth or login flow.
